Subject: On-prem inference orchestration: network & control/data plane alignment

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for taking time on short notice. We're scoping an on-prem deployment of Redwood for a phased rollout across three datacenters. Before we lock the SOW, our network and security teams asked for a reference readout focused on: control-plane isolation (management/control channel), data-plane tenancy (isolation between tenants and model payloads), egress and logging requirements, and the expected firewall / port matrix for staging -> prod cutover.

Specific asks:
- A single-page reference diagram that shows the control plane (Redwood control plane endpoints and proxies) vs the data plane (inference nodes, model caches, KV stores) and how traffic flows.
- Clarify whether the control plane requires outbound connectivity to redwood-managed endpoints or whether it can be fully VPC-peered and customer-controlled.
- Cert rotation approach for mTLS between control plane and inference nodes (we need to show this to our compliance team).
- Expected egress behavior for telemetry: does telemetry flow to a Redwood endpoint or can it be delivered to our Splunk/SIEM?

Can you share a reference diagram + short runbook checklist we can attach to the security review? If we can get a draft by Friday (2028-06-28) that would be ideal. Attaching our internal network matrix for reference.

Regards,
Alicia
Lead Systems Architect
Orion Systems

Subject: Re: On-prem inference orchestration: network & control/data plane alignment

Thanks Alicia — good framing. I've attached an initial single-page reference diagram (orchestration-overview-v1.png) that highlights the control vs data plane and a couple of deployment variants (shared control plane vs customer-managed control plane).

Quick answers up front:
- Control plane connectivity: we support both modes. For the customer-managed mode the control plane is deployed inside the customer VPC (or on-prem) and talks to the data plane over internal networks; for the hosted/managed mode the control plane makes outbound TLS connections to Redwood endpoints (we provide firewall egress IPs and DNS names).
- Cert rotation: we use short-lived mTLS certs rotated via the control plane CA; customers can plug in their KMS/HSM for private key material. We'll include the cert rotation sequence in the runbook.
- Telemetry/egress: telemetry can be delivered to customer endpoints (Splunk/HTTP/GRPC sink) or sent to Redwood telemetry endpoints depending on the deployment choice. We log at token-level only when opted in.

Next step: Kimberly and Aditya — can you review the diagram and the minimum port list I sketched and add the ACL/egress guidance? I'll collate and share the runbook draft by EOD Thursday. Alicia — can you confirm whether Orion wants the control plane inside your VPC or if you prefer Redwood-managed for the initial PoC?

Attachments: orchestration-overview-v1.png (diagram)

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of OnPrem Deployments
Redwood Inference

Appended a few concrete items and an ACL CSV so your network folks can map rules quickly (attached: network-acls.csv). Also pushed a first-pass runbook to the shared drive (runbook-draft.md). Summary below.

Summary / minimums for customer-managed control plane (recommended for Orion PoC):
- Control plane -> Data plane connectivity: mTLS on port 8443 (control RPC), optional port 9400 for diagnostics. All control plane endpoints should be reachable from the data plane subnets; keep an allowlist of control-plane FQDNs when you want outbound-only.
- Data plane inference traffic: internal clients call the local inference gateway on port 8080 (HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2). In multi-tenant setups we recommend sidecar-level tenant tokens and per-tenant cache isolation.
- Egress for telemetry/logs: provide a dedicated egress path to your SIEM collector (port 443) with signed delivery. If you opt for Redwood telemetry, we will provide an egress FQDN and IP range (we can publish a short IP list for firewall rules).
- Cert rotation: control plane CA issues 24-hour short-lived certs by default; we support a 7-day TTL for constrained environments. Rotation flow: control plane requests new leaf cert -> signed by CA -> pushed to data plane agent via existing mTLS channel -> health-check and cert swap. Documented in runbook-draft.md (section 3).
- Network segmentation: separate management subnet for control-plane components (ex: 10.10.100.0/24), data subnets per DC for inference nodes (ex: 10.10.1.0/24, 10.10.2.0/24). Use NSG/ACLs to restrict east-west to only required ports.
- Observability: ensure you accept syslog/HTTPS sinks from the data plane; we emit JSON telemetry with tenant_id, request_id, and sampling markers.

Open questions for Orion team:
1) Do you require NAT egress with a single public IP per DC for outbound control-plane connectivity?
2) Will the SIEM accept mutual TLS ingestion or do you prefer token-authenticated HTTP?

Attachments: network-acls.csv, runbook-draft.md

-Kim
Principal DevOps Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a couple of operational notes from the deployment playbook side:

- Egress & NAT: we typically recommend a configured NAT per-datacenter to simplify firewall rules and make audits easier. If Orion wants per-tenant public IP mapping for billing/audit, that's doable but increases complexity.
- Canary tenant test: before cutting over, run a canary tenant workload that exercises model cache misses and heavy KV operations; observe control-plane latency and token/credential churn.
- Telemetry sink options: we can ship telemetry over HTTPS to your Splunk HEC endpoint with mutual TLS, or deliver via S3/HTTPS pull if you prefer storage-first. We log events at multiple levels — control, request, cache eviction — set your retention accordingly.
- Fallback mode: if the control plane becomes unreachable, data plane will continue to serve from local cache for in-flight requests for up to 10 minutes (configurable). After that, it will enter read-only mode until the control channel recovers. Make sure your monitoring alerts on that threshold.

I've added a short runbook section for the canary and fallback test in the shared drive (see INFRA-8421) and recommended alert thresholds. Suggest we schedule a 60-minute alignment call to walk through the diagram and the ACL CSV with your network/security owners.

-Aditya
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
